title: Turning raw recordings into a research dataset
subtitle: The messy-to-production data work that powers reliable biotech models — cleaning, annotating, and validating neural recordings end to end.
author: Caleb Liu
intro: Neural recordings arrive dirty — bad channels, dropped samples, and mislabeled epochs. A model trained on that data just memorizes the noise, so the first job is never the model, it's the data.

sections.label: Clean → annotate → extract
sections.caption: A three-stage pipeline that turns raw, noisy recordings into a versioned research dataset.

sections.label: The approach
sections.body: I designed an end-to-end data pipeline for cleaning, annotating, and feature-extracting neural recordings — the kind of messy-to-production data work that powers reliable biotech research models.

sections.label: The approach
sections.body: Versioning every stage meant the dataset could be reproduced and audited, so downstream models trained on trustworthy data rather than a one-off export.
The data, not the model, is the hard part — and getting it right is what makes the model honest.
